## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of per-particle loop1 math, combined with a simple scalar loop2, can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 11.908 at N=4000 to 8.055 at N=16000 — overhead amortization below the L2 spill point (N≈60787). From N=65000 (just past L2 spill) through N=4000000, cost stays flat at 7.9–8.0 ns/p with no knee at the L2→DRAM transition. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.05 holds at 8.2–8.8 ns/p, q=0.25 at ~10.0 ns/p, all flat from N=16000 onward. The L1d spill (N≈949) is below the smallest measured N, so its effect is not directly visible. The absence of any spill knee confirms the workload is not cache-pressure-limited.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.73 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algorithm is compute/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: flat ns/p across four orders of magnitude in N shows no streaming regime is ever reached. Death rate degrades bandwidth monotonically — q=0.05 peaks at 8.41 GB/s (33.3%), q=0.25 at 6.95 GB/s (27.6%). The transition is by death rate, not by N: the branchy respawn path (33 `bl` calls to spawn) raises the floor as churn grows.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized loop1 component-wise within a single particle, not across particles: `fmul.4s` and `fadd.4s` operate on four floats packed from one particle's 68-byte stride (`add x9, x9, #0x44`). A gather appears — `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x10]` loads a single element into one lane — confirming the stride-69 layout prevents clean wide loads. `ext.16b` and `mov.s v18[3], v7[0]` reshuffle to assemble a 4-lane vector from non-contiguous components. Loop2 is entirely scalar: 45 `ldrb` and 17 `strb` implement byte-granular scatter with `csel` clamping, and 33 `bl` calls to `_layouts.ML1.data.Data.spawn` dominate the high-churn path. Component-wise vectorization explains the moderate bandwidth; the byte-scatter loop2 caps it.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algorithm never exceeds 8.73 GB/s (34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, and drops to 6.89 GB/s (27.3%) at q=0.25. Component-wise auto-vectorization with a gather (`ld1.s`) and the scalar byte-scatter loop2 (45 `ldrb`, 17 `strb`, 33 `bl` to spawn) prevent any approach to the streaming ceiling, regardless of death rate or N.
